taxonomy_note: Analyst planning lens; reassess actual root cause.

controls.boundary: OS command and argument injection — authoritative consumer
controls.source_trace: Trace executable selection, shell use, argv boundaries, option handling, environment and working directory. Identify what the external utility does with each caller-controlled argument.
controls.controlled_verification: Replace the executable with an inert local argv recorder using the same application construction path. Compare a normal filename with the suspected shell/option-boundary input, then inspect the actual argv and utility semantics. A recorder proves argument construction, not arbitrary command execution by the real utility.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: No shell does not mean no risk: a utility can interpret dangerous options or execute delegated functionality. Conversely, shell punctuation inside a single literal argument is not proof it became shell syntax.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Avoid unnecessary shell parsing, fix executable/option authority and use supported argument separators where the actual utility supports them. Retest normal paths, original boundary case and required options in a bounded replica.

coverage_unit: One primary investigative assertion for this technique; not exhaustive coverage. Expand only for genuinely distinct policy/effect assertions in the actual assessment.
